# Speed up the test cycle — scoped baseline, per-test timing, event-driven reload, non-critical tests to --full

- **Kind**: chore
- **Date**: 2026-07-31
- **Requested by**: Ian

Apply rules: `django-mojo-build-conventions`, `nativemojo-board-conventions`, plus the repo's `.claude/rules/testing.md`, `build-baseline.md`, `git.md`.

## Description

Repo rules mandate whole-suite runs at up to three points per work item, so every task — however small — pays the suite cost repeatedly. Ian: *"Running full tests before every task and after every task is bonkers and adds crazy amount of time."*

Two goals:

1. **Make the test cycle fast**, without losing coverage.
2. **Let the session agent choose the test scope** — proportional to the change, escalating only when warranted.

### Decisions (Ian)

- **Nothing gets deleted.** Non-critical tests move to the `--full` tier; they still run on demand and pre-release.
- **The before-work baseline becomes agent-scoped.**
- **Record how long each individual test takes.** ✅ confirmed.
- **Do NOT reorder modules by measured duration.** ❌ rejected — see D1. These are *base* tests: downstream projects (maestro and others) run them alongside their own, so a runtime duration profile would differ per project and make ordering unpredictable.
- **Move non-critical tests to `--full`.** Reaffirmed after scoping pushed back; see D2.

> **Two rounds of numbers in this workspec were wrong before the third stuck.** The filing claimed ~74 core `server_settings` blocks costing "5.5 minutes of pure sleep"; a first scoping pass corrected that to 6 blocks / 27 s but still misattributed the wall clock. **Only the measurements below are load-bearing.** The lesson is why per-test timing (Phase 2) is in scope: grep counts are not measurements.

### Measured baseline (2026-07-31, `bin/run_tests --agent`, reproduced twice)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| **Suite duration (runner-internal)** | **98.98 s** |
| Tests | 3,152 total — 3,096 passed, **0 failed**, 56 skipped |
| Sum of module durations | 323.26 s across `-j 4` lanes ⇒ theoretical floor 75.6 s |
| Serial tail | 4.62 s (`test_job_engine` 1.4 + `test_metrics` 3.2) |
| Slowest modules | `test_shortlink` **33.7 s** / 64 tests, `test_jobs` 27.4, `test_account` 23.3, `test_auth` 22.8, `test_helpers` 21.1 |

Source: `testproject/var/test_failures.json`. **`VAR_ROOT` is `testproject/var`**, not `./var` — the rules docs, `TESTING.md:28` and `.claude/agents/test-runner.md` all cite the wrong path.

98.98 s is the **runner-internal** span (`testit/runner.py:1286` → `:1141`); it excludes `uv run` startup, interpreter/Django import and the `bin/run_tests` wrapper. Before/after comparisons must use one clock.

### What actually bounds the wall clock — and what that means for trimming

`_collect_modules` (`testit/runner.py:1208-1246`) returns modules **alphabetically** and `main` submits them to a `ThreadPoolExecutor` in that order (`:1434-1441`). `test_shortlink`, the longest module, is submitted 30th of 32 and runs as a tail against idle lanes. A greedy 4-lane simulation in that exact order predicts **98.7 s vs 98.98 s measured (0.30 s error)**.

Reordering is **rejected** (D1). The consequence, stated plainly: ~14 s of idle-lane waste stays, and **the floor is set by the single longest module.** That is the key constraint on Phase 4 — trimming tests only moves the wall clock if it trims *the heavy modules*. Trimming a fast module frees a lane that is already idle.

This is why Phase 3 comes before Phase 4: today `test_shortlink` is 33.7 s of which ~27 s is `time.sleep()`. Remove that and it drops to ~7 s, the longest module becomes `test_jobs` (27.4 s) or `test_account` (23.3 s), and only then does trimming pay.

### `requires_apps` already solves the unused-app case

`testit/runner.py:1368-1381` skips an entire module when a required app is not installed. A downstream project that does not install `mojo.apps.dnsman` never runs `test_dnsman`. So the tiering criterion must **not** be "is this app optional" — that is handled. It is: *within the apps a consumer does use, is this test a critical contract or exhaustive depth?* (D2).

### The `server_settings` cost, correctly counted and attributed

| Module | Contexts entered | Runs in core? |
|---|---|---|
| `test_shortlink` | **6** | Yes — `shortlink.py:644`, `:674`, and `:666` **inside `for value in unsafe:` over a 4-element list** (`:660-666`), so one statement enters 4×. |
| `test_helpers` | 2 | Yes, but **stubbed** — `tests/test_helpers/test_server_conf.py:54-55` rebinds `th._SLEEP`/`th._POLL` to no-ops. Zero real cost. |
| `test_auth` | 1 | Yes — only `handoff.py:436`; `:40`, `:399`, `:432` are comments. |
| `test_dnsman` | 1 | Yes — `12_config.py:72`. |
| `test_assistant` | 15 | **No** — all in `3_test_live_assistant.py`, `@th.requires_extra("slow")`. |
| `test_security` | 10 | **No** — module is `requires_extra: ["slow"]`. |
| `test_incident` | 1 | **No** — opt-in. |

**Core total: 8 contexts ≈ 36 s**, six of them in `test_shortlink` (~80% of that module's runtime). Modules run as **threads in one process** (`ThreadPoolExecutor`, `:1434`), so a sleeping thread yields — those 36 s are *module* time, worth ~12-14 s of makespan. Any "N seconds of sleep in a 99 s run" claim is a category error.

### Why the sleep exists — do not replace it with the existing poll

`_poll_server_up` (`testit/helpers.py:728`) issues `GET /` and returns on **any** response; it cannot tell the old worker from the new one. The 3 s exit sleep exists precisely so the **old** worker (still holding the overrides) has exited before the poll can answer (`testit/helpers.py:841-846`). Swapping it for that poll reintroduces the stale-override bug behind #543.

Verified: uvicorn runs a **reloader parent** plus **one worker** spawned via `multiprocessing.spawn`; a reload kills the worker and spawns a new PID that re-imports settings fresh. `load_settings_config()` (`mojo/helpers/settings/parser.py:141`) is the single choke point where a process reads `var/django.conf`. So *(new PID + config fingerprint)* is a sound discriminator — in the single-worker case, which is all `bin/asgi_local` produces.

## Plan

### Objective

Cut the per-task test cost from up to three whole-suite runs to one scoped run plus one targeted verification, and shrink the default suite itself — with **zero loss of coverage**, since nothing is deleted and everything still runs under `--full`.

### Design decisions

**D1 — No duration-based reordering.** Rejected by Ian: these are base tests that downstream projects run alongside their own, so a measured-duration profile would be per-project, unstable, and make ordering unpredictable. Accepted as-is. Consequence recorded honestly in Context: ~14 s of idle-lane waste remains and the wall clock stays bounded by the longest single module — which is exactly why Phase 3 precedes Phase 4.

**D2 — Tier by criticality, not by speed or app.** `requires_apps` already skips modules for uninstalled apps, so optional-app coverage is not the axis. The criterion, to be written into the testit docs:
- **Default tier (critical):** security boundaries (permissions, auth, tenant isolation, secrets); core framework contracts (model save/serialize, REST dispatch, graphs, `request.DATA`); regression tests for previously-shipped bugs; anything whose failure means the framework is broken for every consumer.
- **`--full` tier (extended):** exhaustive input-validation matrices beyond the first representative case; deep feature-internal variants of a single app; tests duplicating coverage asserted elsewhere; slow live-service tests.
Because `--full` currently means `--extra slow`, add a second extra — `extended` — and make `--full` imply **both**. Keeps "slow" meaning slow and "extended" meaning non-critical, instead of overloading one word.

**D3 — The readiness signal is a file written by the generated `_asgi.py`, not a framework endpoint.** `bin/create_testproject:55-61` generates `testproject/bin/_asgi.py`. Writing `var/asgi_ready.json` = `{"pid", "conf"}` at module import gives the same discriminator with none of the costs of a REST route: nothing ships to consumer projects, no gating flag, no exposure question. Decisively, an HTTP probe whose own registration depends on the settings under test fails exactly when it is most needed — `mojo/urls.py` builds urlpatterns at import from `get_static(...)`. A lifespan hook is not an option: `testproject/var/asgi.log` reports *"ASGI 'lifespan' protocol appears unsupported"*.

**D4 — Fingerprint captured at `load_settings_config()`, nowhere else.** `mojo/helpers/settings/parser.py:141` is the one place a process reads `var/django.conf`; a hash taken later would describe a file the process is not serving under.

**D5 — `_SETTINGS_SERIALIZE` stays.** Modules are threads in one process and a settings override is global process state; two concurrent contexts would interleave regardless of reload speed. Make each turn cheap, don't remove the queue.

**D6 — Dropped: keeping the server warm.** `bin/run_tests:26-31,44-46` only stops a server **it** started, so when one is already up the change buys nothing. Worse, uvicorn watches the whole repo root (`asgi.log` line 1), so a warm server restarts on every `.py` edit between runs; and `_run_migrations` (`bin/asgi_local:85`) is the only per-invocation `migrate`. Measured full restart: 2.43 s — not worth these trades.

**D7 — Rejected: in-process settings mutation.** `mojo/urls.py:5,15-16` reads `get_static("MOJO_API_MODULE")`/`REST_AUTO_PREFIX` at import and `load_mojo_modules()` runs at import, so in-process overrides would leave routing stale and tests would pass against configuration that never existed. It also adds a live settings-mutation surface.

### Implementation steps

**Phase 1 — policy and vocabulary** (docs only)

1. Rewrite `.claude/rules/build-baseline.md`: default baseline = affected modules (`bin/run_tests --agent -t <module> ...`); the mapping recipe (changed path → owning app → `tests/test_<app>`, plus known dependents, widen when unsure); the escalation triggers from Acceptance; unchanged invariants (record the baseline, green-before ⇒ green-after, stop on red). Fix the report path.
2. Update `.claude/agents/test-runner.md`: accept a scope, default to scoped, stop being a third whole-suite run, fix the report path and the `error.log` path at `:73`.
3. Vocabulary sweep — "full suite" ⇒ "whole suite" (default tier) vs `--full` (extended tier): `AI_DEV.md:63,101,189`, `.claude/rules/testing.md:25`, `TESTING.md`, `CLAUDE.md`.
4. Update the workspace rule `django-mojo-build-conventions` via `upsert_workspace_doc` so the post-build trio matches.

**Phase 2 — per-test timing**

5. `testit/helpers.py` `_run_unit()` (`:177+`): time `func(...)`, pass elapsed into `_record_result()` on every exit path (passed/skipped/failed/error); add `duration` to the record (`:274-283`).
6. `testit/runner.py` agent report (`:1100-1160`): add a `slowest` list (top ~25). Fix `:1101` to read `var/logs/error.log`.

**Phase 3 — `server_settings` reload**

7. `mojo/helpers/settings/parser.py`: in `load_settings_config()`, after `load_config`, compute `sha256` of the raw config bytes into a module-level `CONF_FINGERPRINT`.
8. `bin/create_testproject` (`:55-61`): extend the generated `_asgi.py` to write `var/asgi_ready.json` = `{"pid": os.getpid(), "conf": CONF_FINGERPRINT}` at module import, after `create_application()`. Write atomically (temp + `os.replace`).
9. `testit/helpers.py`:
   - `_read_ready()` → `(pid, conf)` or `None` when the **file is absent** (⇒ fall back) — distinct from stale/partial contents (⇒ keep waiting).
   - `_wait_for_worker(expected_sha, exclude_pid, timeout)` → poll ~0.1 s until `conf == expected_sha and pid != exclude_pid`, **then** confirm the socket serves via `_POLL` (`:728`). Raise on timeout with pid/fingerprint in the message.
   - `_conf_apply`/`_conf_restore` (`:691-708`): report whether content actually changed; **skip the write when unchanged**.
   - `server_settings()` (`:805+`): read the signal before writing; unchanged content ⇒ no write, no wait; otherwise wait on entry and exit. Delete both `_SLEEP` calls. Assert single-worker and document the limitation.
   - Keep the `_SLEEP`/`_POLL` seams — `tests/test_helpers/test_server_conf.py` rebinds them; update that file.
10. Fix the `tests/test_metrics/__init__.py` comment (keep the flag). Diagnose the stray `AUTH_CSP_ENABLED`.

**Phase 4 — re-tier**

11. Add the `extended` extra: `--full` implies `slow` **and** `extended` (`testit/runner.py:380,398`). Delete `-q/--quick` and its `quick_` discovery (`:356`, `:478-480`, `:522`, `:574`) plus the `TESTING.md:31` line documenting it.
12. Using Phase 2's slowest-N output, work **the heavy modules first** (`test_jobs`, `test_account`, `test_auth`, `test_helpers`, `test_dnsman`, and `test_shortlink` post-Phase-3). For each, apply D2's criterion and tag non-critical tests `@th.requires_extra("extended")` — or the whole file where a file is uniformly extended.
13. Write the criterion into `docs/django_developer/testit/Overview.md` so future tests are tagged at authoring time rather than re-audited later.
14. Record default-tier count/wall-clock and `--full` count/wall-clock before and after.

### Edge cases and error handling

- **Signal file absent** → fall back to sleeps; never hard-fail a consumer project.
- **Worker mid-restart** (stale file, socket refusing) → keep waiting inside the bounded window; never treat as "absent".
- **Byte-identical restore** → no write, no wait.
- **Reload never fires** → bounded wait raises loudly with the expected fingerprint.
- **Multiple workers** → `pid != exclude_pid` could be satisfied by a different un-restarted worker, reintroducing #543. `bin/asgi_local` starts one worker; assert it and document.
- **Concurrent test runs** → still forbidden (one port, one shared Postgres); `var/testit.lock` guards it.
- **Re-tiering hides a real regression** → mitigated by D2 keeping all security/permission/regression tests in the default tier, and by `--full` remaining mandatory pre-publish.
- **Scoped baseline picks wrong modules** → mitigated by conservative escalation; the post-change run catches it.

### Testing plan

- **Baseline before any edit**: `bin/run_tests --agent`. Known-good: **3,152 / 3,096 passed / 0 failed / 56 skipped / 98.98 s**. Do not build on red.
- **This item changes `testit/` ⇒ framework-wide blast radius ⇒ the whole suite is the correct scope for its own verification** — a worked example of the rule Phase 1 introduces. `--full` too, since Phase 4 changes what `--full` selects.
- Phase 3 tests in `tests/test_helpers/test_server_conf.py`: stale-override regression (must fail against poll-only); no-op write performs no wait; signal-absent falls back; timeout raises; mid-restart not mistaken for absent.
- Phase 2: records carry non-negative `duration`; `slowest` present; `server_log_tail` populates on an induced 500.
- Phase 4: **default + `--full` test counts must sum to today's total** — that is the proof nothing was deleted. Assert it explicitly.
- Known flakes not to mistake for regressions: #1004 (`test_docit.hybrid_search_ranking`), #274, #275.
- Iterate with `bin/run_tests --agent -t test_helpers`; close with a whole-suite run and a `--full` run.

### Challenge

Independent red-team (fresh context, repo read access); every objection verified in-repo before disposition. Ian then reviewed and overrode two conclusions — recorded at the end.

- **"The bottleneck is module submission order, not sleeps."** — **verified, then overtaken by D1.** Durations sum to 323.26 s; `test_shortlink` is submitted 30th of 32; greedy 4-lane simulation in that order predicts **98.7 s vs 98.98 s measured (0.30 s error)**; longest-first predicts 84.4 s. Ian rejected reordering (base tests shared with downstream projects). The finding is retained as *analysis* because it explains why trimming only pays on heavy modules — which now shapes Phase 4.
- **"'27 s of sleep in a 99 s run' is a category error — modules are threads, a sleeper yields."** — **amended.** Verified `ThreadPoolExecutor` at `testit/runner.py:1434`. ~36 s of module time ≈ 12-14 s of makespan.
- **"The call-site inventory is wrong in both directions."** — **amended.** `test_shortlink/shortlink.py:666` sits inside a 4-element loop ⇒ **6** contexts, not 3; `test_auth` has **1**, not 2. Core total **8 ≈ 36 s**.
- **"A framework REST endpoint is the wrong home for test-only infra."** — **amended, adopted in full** as D3. The decisive argument: an HTTP probe whose own registration depends on the settings under test fails exactly when needed. Also verified a lifespan hook would not fire.
- **"'Probe absent' and 'worker mid-restart' are indistinguishable."** — **amended**; now an explicit criterion, handled naturally by the file-based design.
- **"`pid != exclude_pid` assumes one worker."** — **amended**; explicit single-worker assertion + documented limitation.
- **"Warm server buys ~zero and breaks things."** — **amended: phase dropped** (D6).
- **"98.98 s is the runner-internal span."** — **amended**; called out so before/after use one clock.
- **"Confirm which command Ian was actually running."** — **resolved.** Ian identified the real cause: repo *rules* mandating whole-suite runs. Located: `build-baseline.md:9` (before), `:23` (after), `test-runner.md:16` (post-build agent) — up to three per item — plus a vocabulary bug where the default run is called "the full test suite". Phase 1 now targets the rules directly, which is a better fix than the one scoping proposed.
- **"Dropping the trim reverses an explicit instruction."** — **objection upheld; scoping's reversal withdrawn.** Ian reaffirmed the trim as a move to `--full`. Reinstated as Phase 4 with a written criterion (D2), sequenced after Phase 3 so it targets modules that are still heavy once the dead sleeps are gone.
- **One challenger claim rejected on verification:** it called `tests/test_metrics/__init__.py`'s `serial: True` stale. The *comment* is wrong (`fanout.py:150-169` uses no `server_settings`), but the flag is accidentally load-bearing — the module writes `dj_settings` directly, a process-global mutation that would race sibling lanes. **Fix the comment, keep the flag.**
- **Judged sound, no change:** D7, the PID+fingerprint discriminator closing #543 in the single-worker case, `_SETTINGS_SERIALIZE` being load-bearing, `--quick` being dead, and per-test timing being real work.

## Investigation

- **What exists**:
  - `testit/runner.py` — `_collect_modules` (1208-1246), pool submission (1434-1441), `-j` default (404-410), `--quick` (356) + `quick_` discovery (478-480, 522, 574), `--full`→`--extra slow` (380, 398), `requires_apps` skip (1368-1381), `requires_extra` (119, 1385+), serial scheduling (1350-1360, 1450, 1517), agent report (1100-1160), `error.log` path bug (1101), `_LOCK_FILE` (22).
  - `testit/helpers.py` — `server_settings()` (~805), `_conf_apply`/`_conf_restore` (691-708), `_poll_server_up` (728), `_SLEEP`/`_POLL` seams (742-743), `_SETTINGS_SERIALIZE` (750), `_run_unit()` (177+), `_record_result()` (271-293), `requires_extra` decorator.
  - `mojo/helpers/settings/parser.py` — `load_settings_config()` (141). `mojo/helpers/settings/helper.py` — `get()` (157) vs `get_static()` (180).
  - `bin/create_testproject` — `_asgi.py` (55-61), `urls.py` (274), `django.conf` (318).
  - `bin/run_tests` (`sleep 3` :29, conditional teardown :26-31/:44-46), `bin/asgi_local` (`_run_migrations` :85, uvicorn `--reload-include '*.conf'` :128-129).
  - Policy: `.claude/rules/build-baseline.md`, `.claude/rules/testing.md`, `.claude/agents/test-runner.md`, `AI_DEV.md`, `TESTING.md`, workspace rule `django-mojo-build-conventions`.
- **What changes**: baseline policy + the three whole-suite mandates; per-test timing; `server_settings` waits on a real readiness signal; non-critical tests move to a new `extended` tier under `--full`; several doc/report defects.
- **Constraints**:
  - One test run at a time — one port, one shared Postgres (`.claude/rules/git.md`). No worktrees, no parallel suite-running agents.
  - `testproject/` is regenerated by `bin/create_testproject` — change the generator, never the generated file.
  - django-mojo ships testit **and these base tests** to downstream projects, which run them alongside their own. No per-project state, no consumer-facing surface, and the default tier must stay meaningful for a consumer verifying the framework.
  - Wall clock is bounded by the longest single module (D1) — trimming must target heavy modules to matter.
- **Related files**: `testit/runner.py`, `testit/helpers.py`, `mojo/helpers/settings/parser.py`, `bin/create_testproject`, `bin/run_tests`, `bin/asgi_local`, `tests/test_helpers/test_server_conf.py`, `tests/test_metrics/__init__.py`, `.claude/rules/build-baseline.md`, `.claude/rules/testing.md`, `.claude/agents/test-runner.md`, `AI_DEV.md`, `TESTING.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/django_developer/testit/Overview.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Out of scope**:
  - Deleting tests or weakening assertions.
  - Reordering modules by duration (D1); keeping the server warm (D6).
  - Editing `.claude/skills/maestro-build/SKILL.md` (upstream-managed).
  - Rewriting the 8 `server_settings` call sites — fix the mechanism. (Collapsing `test_shortlink`'s 4-iteration loop into one context would save ~13 s but weakens a security regression test; leave it.)
  - Changing what the opt-in `slow` modules contain (`test_incident`, `test_security`, live-assistant).
